should: Evaluate this accessibility patch for Drupal core with before and after axe scans and tell me whether it introduces regressions.
Which Drupal core modules should I test first to find accessibility regressions when they are enabled?
How do I give a recurring axe violation a stable ID so I can deduplicate it across pages and track it between test runs?
Which of the 100 Drupal accessibility user stories are already automated in Playwright, and which should I automate next?
should_not: Write a PHPUnit kernel test for my contrib module's service.
How do I announce an AJAX update to screen reader users in a Drupal behavior?
How do I configure Search API boosting for a number field?
Explain how to set up OAuth2 scopes with simple_oauth for a mobile app.
I want to reproduce Drupal core issue 3155130 in the lab and compare before and after side by side.

cases.prompt: The same button.submit has a button-name violation on /user/login, /contact and /user/register at desktop width. How do I compute the stable IDs, and how many of each do I get?
expected: computes instance_id as SHA-256 of page path, selector, rule ID and screen type, giving three distinct instance IDs
computes pattern_id as SHA-256 of selector, rule ID and screen type (independent of page path), giving one pattern ID
reports it as 1 pattern with 3 instances
grounded_in: // Stable: same selector + rule + screen type = same pattern

cases.prompt: A patch fixed 3 violations in the patched scan but also introduced 2 new ones elsewhere. What status should the evaluation report and what is the next step?
expected: reports status MIXED (fixes some, introduces others)
says a trade-off analysis is needed rather than calling it a clean PASS
lists the new violations explicitly with their instance and pattern IDs
must_not: declares the patch PASS or ready to merge

cases.prompt: Walk me through evaluating an accessibility patch end to end so the before and after comparison is fair.
expected: starts with a baseline scan on unpatched Drupal fetched from git, recording violations_baseline
applies the patch, clears caches and verifies it applied with no rejections
runs the same axe-core scan on the same pages for the patched scan
computes fixed, added and unchanged violations and writes Markdown, JSON and HTML reports
grounded_in: 1. Run same axe-core scan on same pages

cases.prompt: I scanned at 768px wide. Is that mobile or desktop for the violation ID?
expected: says desktop, because mobile is under 768px and desktop is 768px or wider
notes screen type is part of the hash inputs for the IDs

cases.prompt: Draft the required fields for an accessibility bug report on a login button with no accessible name.
expected: includes violation IDs (instance_id and pattern_id), URL, XPath (simplified and full) and HTML snippet
includes the WCAG success criterion and rule ID, severity (critical/high/medium/low) and frequency (single_page/pattern/systematic)
includes context: screen_type, color_mode and theme, plus steps to reproduce

cases.prompt: I enabled views_ui and my 18 Tier 1 workflows now show 12 added violations compared with baseline. How serious is that and what do I record?
expected: rates the impact High because 10-20 added violations means significant regressions needing fixes before release
records impact as fixed minus added
disables the module and restores baseline state after the test
grounded_in: | **High** | 10–20 | Significant regressions; needs fixes before release |

cases.prompt: I only have time to test a few core modules for accessibility. Which categories should I prioritise, and which should I skip?
expected: puts experimental modules (e.g. layout_builder, workspaces, big_pipe) first as high risk needing full workflow testing
gives optional modules (search, comment, taxonomy, media) medium priority with targeted feature testing
spot-checks core modules only
skips test_only modules, which are never enabled in real sites
grounded_in: Modules in active development; likely to introduce regressions.
Modules used only for testing; never enable in actual Drupal sites.

cases.prompt: How do I establish the baseline before measuring a single module's accessibility impact?
expected: starts from a fresh Drupal install with experimental and optional modules disabled
runs the 18 Tier 1 workflows as an accessibility scan and records the baseline violation count
notes core modules are always enabled

cases.prompt: My scan found a focus-visible violation on all buttons. Should I file it on drupal.org right away?
expected: says to search for existing issues first by exact XPath, pattern ID, rule ID and WCAG criterion
files as a pattern-level issue (systematic frequency) rather than many per-page issues
references the user story ID, e.g. 3.9 Form Field Focus - Focus Indicator Visible

cases.prompt: I'm adding a Playwright test for the password reset flow (story 1.3). How should I name it and tie it back to the story?
expected: puts the story ID at the front of the test name, such as '1.3: Password Reset Flow'
links the test to the story definition in USER-STORIES.md and updates the coverage matrix
runs it by story ID prefix with npx playwright test --grep
grounded_in: Reference story ID in test name:

cases.prompt: What themes, colour modes and viewports should the accessibility workflow tests cover?
expected: lists themes Olivero, Claro and default_admin
covers light mode and dark mode via prefers-color-scheme
covers desktop 1280×1024, tablet 768×1024 and mobile 375×812

cases.prompt: Explain how the 100 accessibility user stories are tiered and where I should invest automation first.
expected: describes 30 Tier 1 critical, 30 Tier 2 important and 40 Tier 3 extended stories across 10 functional areas
says Tier 1 workflows (authentication, content creation, forms, navigation) must work for all users and are the automation priority
states Tier 1 automation goal is 100%
grounded_in: Essential user journeys that **must work** for all users.
